title: Plug a tubeless tire puncture
summary: Make a roadside repair with a string plug kit to get home or to a shop.
tools: Tubeless plug kit (reamer and insertion tool)

steps.text: Find the leak. Spray soapy water on the tread and look for bubbles if you can't see the object.
Mark the spot, then pull out the nail or object with pliers.
steps.caution: Only tread punctures up to about 6 mm can be plugged. A sidewall or shoulder cut needs a new tire.

steps.text: Push the reamer into the hole and work it in and out a few times to clean and roughen it.
Thread a string through the insertion tool so it's centered, coated in the kit's cement if supplied.
Push the tool in until about a third of the string is left outside, then pull the tool straight out quickly. The string stays in.
Trim the string about 5 mm above the tread and inflate the tire to the pressure on your spec sheet.
Check the plug with soapy water. Ride gently and have the tire patched from the inside or replaced soon.
steps.caution: A string plug is a temporary fix. Keep speeds moderate and avoid carrying a passenger until the tire is properly repaired.
